question: Under one added rule, that swapping the listed order of two distinctions that both hold 1 costs a factor s = -1 (control +1), do the growth law's own free commit orders supply the sign of the three-detector experiment with the real Z and X readings held fixed?
forbidden_inputs: No assigned sign pattern, chosen preparation wiring, complex phase or postselection may enter the preparation. The production growth routine decides the children; the swap rule decides the signs. The readers' reference listing is a declared scaffold under reading R1 only.
primary_observable: Full GHZ contradiction with fixed real readings: every even-size correlation c(T) = <X_T Z_rest> is +-1 and T -> c(T) is not a character (n = 3: <ZZZ><XXZ><XZX><ZXX> = -1).
cheapest_meaningful_control: s = +1 in place of -1; the order-blind average R1b; readers born in the same round R3; the rule applied to the readings JW; reading the old distinction alone.
first_executable_signal: Time the ternary census and its gate before the knot census and the growth fixtures.
resource_budget: One process, exact integers, at most 720 orders of one knot and 5,040 commit orders of growth fixtures up to seven knots; expected under a minute, 1 GiB memory.
stop_rule: Stop after the gate, P1-P7 and the declared scaffold variations. Success only if a full contradiction follows from growth reorderings and the rule with nothing but the settings supplied under a reading other than R1; otherwise name what must be supplied.
decision_or_followup_rule: A contradiction under R1b, R2, R3 or JW reopens the line as a native source; otherwise record the supplied relative inversion as the phase reference and stop the order line.
nonclaims: No claim about physical fermions, exchange statistics as distinct from one CZ per crossing, physical time, or any growth law other than the fewest-funded parity round with its free commit order.
